sections.theory:
Suspension of five-year economic plans

After the period of the eighth plan ended in June 1998, the process of making further five-year plans stopped, a few reasons for which are these:

• instability of the government;

• Pakistan’s atom bomb blast in May 1998;

• enforcement of governor’s rule in Sindh in October 1998;

• protest demonstrations of political parties opposed to the government during 1999;

• dismissal of the Nawaz Sharif government by General Pervez Musharraf on 12 October 1999;

• the crashing of aircraft into America’s World Trade Center on 11 September 2001;

• America’s attack on Afghanistan on 7 October 2001, etc.

Because of these reasons the government could not pay attention towards making plans. However, after this the government made a five-year plan for 2005 to 2010, which is mentioned further on.

Medium-term development plan (Medium Term Development Framework MTDF)

The Pakistan Planning Commission (Planning Commission) prepared a five-year plan, July 2005 to June 2010. This is a form of the “strategy document for poverty reduction” (Poverty Reduction Strategy Paper), which actually consists of annual plans (Annual Plans), so that in view of changes in conditions the required amendment (Adjustment) can be made in it. This framework is in reality part of a twenty-five-year long-term (Long Term) vision (Vision) for 2005 to 2030, whose objective is that, by rapid use of the country’s resources and continuous development efforts, Pakistan be made an extremely developed, industrialised and prosperous country.

Aims and objectives of the plan

The basic objectives of this plan are as follows:

1. Such a just and durable economic system be established from which poverty decreases.

2. To make Pakistan a developed country industrially in the next twenty-five years, such an economy be established which is efficient, balanced, possesses competitive strength at the international level, and is of a high grade technologically (Technologically).

3. The development of the different areas of Pakistan be on equal and just foundations.

4. The right of every citizen to progress be fully protected, especially the rights of children (Children), youths, women and minorities.

Targets of the plan (Targets)

In this plan the following targets have been kept in view:

1. National production

In this period the average annual rate of growth (Growth) of gross national product (G.D.P) will be 7.6 per cent, while in 2009-10 this rate will become 8.2 per cent.

Suspension of five-year economic plans

After the period of the eighth plan ended in June 1998, the process of making further five-year plans stopped, a few reasons for which are these:

• instability of the government;

• Pakistan’s atom bomb blast in May 1998;

• enforcement of governor’s rule in Sindh in October 1998;

• protest demonstrations of political parties opposed to the government during 1999;

• dismissal of the Nawaz Sharif government by General Pervez Musharraf on 12 October 1999;

• the crashing of aircraft into America’s World Trade Center on 11 September 2001;

• America’s attack on Afghanistan on 7 October 2001, etc.

Because of these reasons the government could not pay attention towards making plans. However, after this the government made a five-year plan for 2005 to 2010, which is mentioned further on.

Medium-term development plan (Medium Term Development Framework MTDF)

The Pakistan Planning Commission (Planning Commission) prepared a five-year plan, July 2005 to June 2010. This is a form of the “strategy document for poverty reduction” (Poverty Reduction Strategy Paper), which actually consists of annual plans (Annual Plans), so that in view of changes in conditions the required amendment (Adjustment) can be made in it. This framework is in reality part of a twenty-five-year long-term (Long Term) vision (Vision) for 2005 to 2030, whose objective is that, by rapid use of the country’s resources and continuous development efforts, Pakistan be made an extremely developed, industrialised and prosperous country.

Aims and objectives of the plan

The basic objectives of this plan are as follows:

1. Such a just and durable economic system be established from which poverty decreases.

2. To make Pakistan a developed country industrially in the next twenty-five years, such an economy be established which is efficient, balanced, possesses competitive strength at the international level, and is of a high grade technologically (Technologically).

3. The development of the different areas of Pakistan be on equal and just foundations.

4. The right of every citizen to progress be fully protected, especially the rights of children (Children), youths, women and minorities.

Targets of the plan (Targets)

In this plan the following targets have been kept in view:

1. National production

In this period the average annual rate of growth (Growth) of gross national product (G.D.P) will be 7.6 per cent, while in 2009-10 this rate will become 8.2 per cent.

paras.text: 2. Investment
paras.urdu: 2۔ سرمایہ کاری:
paras.pashto: 2. پانګونه

paras.text: In the five-year period total investment (Investment) of eight trillion (i.e. eighty kharab) rupees will be required, which will increase from 16.8 per cent of GDP in 2004-05 to 20.7 per cent in 2009-10. Sixty-five per cent of investment will be in the private sector (Private Sector) and thirty-five per cent in the government sector (Public Sector). 88.3 per cent of this investment will consist of the internal savings (Internal Savings) of the country and twelve per cent of foreign resources (Foreign Resources).

2. Investment

In the five-year period total investment (Investment) of eight trillion (i.e. eighty kharab) rupees will be required, which will increase from 16.8 per cent of GDP in 2004-05 to 20.7 per cent in 2009-10. Sixty-five per cent of investment will be in the private sector (Private Sector) and thirty-five per cent in the government sector (Public Sector). 88.3 per cent of this investment will consist of the internal savings (Internal Savings) of the country and twelve per cent of foreign resources (Foreign Resources).

3. Balance of foreign payments (Balance of Foreign Payments)

To make the balance of foreign payments better, during the plan an effort will be made that variety and diversification (Diversification) be created in exports. Further, stability be created in the rate of exchange (Exchange Rate), and the ability to compete be created in exports (Exports).

4. Public sector development programme (PSDP)

Under the development programme of the government sector, investment of a total of 2042 billion rupees will be made. As it were, compared with 2004-05, in 2009-10 this will increase threefold and will be 6.3 per cent of GDP. This sum will be spent on these sectors: energy, communications, news-giving, water resources, education, vocational training, public health, physical (Physical) planning and housing.

5. Poverty reduction

At this time one-third (i.e. 33 per cent) of the total population of Pakistan is living below the poverty line (Poverty Line). Under the new plan, by 2010 a reduction of twenty-one per cent will be made in poverty, and in this connection too the following strategy will be adopted:

1. Stress on schemes for getting employment for the poor.

2. Increase in the rate of economic growth (Growth Rate) of the sectors of agriculture, small businesses and construction.

3. Stress on programmes of relief for the poor in connection with Khushhal Pakistan, Tameer-e-Pakistan and drought etc.

4. Issuing small loans (Micro Credits) to agriculture and small businesses.

5. Social protection.

6. More attention to the development of human resources (Human Resources), i.e. education and health.

7. Allotting government lands to landless (Landless) rural people.

6. Housing

At this time in Pakistan there are sixty lakh houses fewer than needed, and by 2010 the need for a further thirty lakh houses will arise. As it were, every year the need for five lakh seventy thousand more houses arises, whereas only three lakh new houses are prepared annually. Therefore during the plan an effort will be made that:

1. The provision of long-term loans at a fixed rate through financial institutions for the construction of houses be made easy.

2. Small residential plots be prepared for people with low income.

3. The technology of house construction be made better.

پانچ سالہ عرصہ میں مجموعی سرمایہ کاری (Investment) آٹھ ٹریلین (یعنی اسی کھرب) روپے درکار ہوگی جو 2004-05ء میں جی ڈی پی کے 16.8 فیصد سے بڑھ کر 2009-10ء میں 20.7 فیصد ہو جائے گی۔ پینسٹھ فیصد سرمایہ کاری نجی شعبہ (Private Sector) میں ہوگی اور پینتیس فیصد سرکاری شعبہ (Public Sector) میں۔ اس سرمایہ کاری کا 88.3 فیصد ملک کی اندرونی بچتوں (Internal Savings) پر مشتمل ہوگا اور بارہ فیصد بیرونی ذرائع (Foreign Resources) پر۔

3۔ بیرونی ادائیگیوں کا توازن: (Balance of Foreign Payments)

بیرونی ادائیگیوں کے توازن کو بہتر بنانے کے لیے منصوبے کے دوران کوشش کی جائے گی کہ برآمدات میں نیرنگی اور تنوع (Diversification) پیدا کی جائے۔ نیز شرحِ مبادلہ (Exchange Rate) میں استحکام اور برآمدات (Exports) میں مقابلہ کی صلاحیت پیدا کی جائے۔

4۔ سرکاری شعبہ میں ترقیاتی پروگرام: (PSDP)

سرکاری شعبہ کے ترقیاتی پروگرام کے تحت کل 2042 بلین روپے کی سرمایہ کاری کی جائے گی۔ گویا 2004-5ء کے مقابلہ میں 2009-10ء میں یہ تین گنا بڑھ جائے گی اور جی ڈی پی کا 6.3 فیصد ہوگی۔ یہ رقم ان شعبوں پر خرچ ہوگی: توانائی، مواصلات، خبر رسانی، آبی ذرائع، تعلیم، پیشہ ورانہ ٹریننگ، صحتِ عامہ، طبعی (Physical) منصوبہ بندی اور مکانات۔

5۔ تخفیفِ غربت:

اس وقت پاکستان کی کل آبادی کا ایک تہائی (یعنی 33 فیصد) خطِ غربت (Poverty Line) سے نیچے زندگی گزار رہا ہے۔ نئے منصوبہ کے تحت 2010ء تک تخفیفِ غربت میں اکیس فیصد کمی کی جائے گی اور اس سلسلہ میں بھی درج ذیل حکمتِ عملی اختیار کی جائے گی:

1۔ غرباء کو روزگار دلانے کی سکیموں پر زور۔

2۔ زراعت، چھوٹے کاروباروں اور تعمیرات کے شعبوں کی معاشی نمو کی شرح (Growth Rate) میں اضافہ۔

3۔ خوشحال پاکستان، تعمیرِ پاکستان اور خشک سالی کے سلسلہ میں غرباء کو ریلیف، وغیرہ پروگراموں پر زور۔

4۔ زراعت اور چھوٹے کاروباروں کو چھوٹے قرضوں (Micro Credits) کا اجراء۔

5۔ معاشرتی تحفظ۔

6۔ انسانی وسائل (Human Resources) کی ترقی یعنی تعلیم و صحت پر زیادہ توجہ۔

7۔ بے زمین (Landless) دیہاتی لوگوں کو سرکاری زمینیں الاٹ کرنا۔

6۔ رہائشی مکانات:

اس وقت پاکستان میں ضرورت سے ساٹھ لاکھ مکانات کم ہیں اور 2010ء تک مزید تیس لاکھ مکانات کی ضرورت پیدا ہو جائے گی۔ گویا ہر سال پانچ لاکھ ستر ہزار مزید مکانات کی ضرورت پڑتی ہے جبکہ صرف تین لاکھ نئے مکانات سالانہ تیار ہوتے ہیں۔ چنانچہ منصوبہ کے دوران کوشش کی جائے گی کہ:

1۔ تعمیرِ مکانات کے لیے مالی اداروں کی معرفت معینہ شرح پر طویل المیعاد قرضوں کی بہم رسانی آسان بنائی جائے۔

2۔ کم آمدنی والے لوگوں کے لیے چھوٹے رہائشی پلاٹ تیار کیے جائیں۔

3۔ تعمیرِ مکانات کی ٹیکنالوجی کو بہتر بنایا جائے۔

د بهرنیو تادیو د توازن د ښه کولو لپاره به د پلان په ترڅ کې هڅه وشي چې په صادراتو کې رنګارنګي او تنوع (Diversification) پیدا شي. همداسې د تبادلې په نرخ (Exchange Rate) کې ثبات او په صادراتو (Exports) کې د سیالۍ وړتیا پیدا شي.

4. په دولتي برخه کې پراختیايي پروګرام (PSDP)

اوس د پاکستان د ټول نفوس درېیمه برخه (یعنې ۳۳ سلنه) د بېوزلۍ له کرښې (Poverty Line) لاندې ژوند کوي. د نوي پلان لاندې به تر ۲۰۱۰ پورې په بېوزلۍ کې یوویشت سلنه کمښت راشي، او په دې برخه کې به لاندې تګلاره غوره شي:

1. بېوزلو ته د روزګار د برابرولو پر طرحو ټینګار.

2. د کرنې، وړو کاروبارونو او ودانیو د برخو د اقتصادي ودې په نرخ (Growth Rate) کې زیاتوالی.

3. د خوشحال پاکستان، تعمیر پاکستان او وچکالۍ په اړه بېوزلو ته د اسانتیا پر پروګرامونو ټینګار.

4. کرنې او وړو کاروبارونو ته د وړو پورونو (Micro Credits) جاري کول.

5. ټولنیزه ساتنه.

6. د بشري سرچینو (Human Resources) پرمختګ یعنې زده‌کړې او روغتیا ته ډېر پام.

7. بې‌ځمکو (Landless) کلیوالو خلکو ته دولتي ځمکې ورکول.

اوس په پاکستان کې له اړتیا شپېته لکه کورونه کم دي، او تر ۲۰۱۰ پورې به د نورو دېرش لکو کورونو اړتیا پیدا شي. ګواکې هر کال د پنځه لکه اویا زره نورو کورونو اړتیا وي، حال دا چې یوازې درې لکه نوي کورونه کلنی جوړېږي. نو د پلان په ترڅ کې به هڅه وشي چې:

1. د کورونو د جوړولو لپاره د مالي ادارو له لارې په ټاکلي نرخ د اوږدمهاله پورونو برابرول اسانه شي.

2. د لږ عاید لرونکو خلکو لپاره واړه استوګنځي پلاټونه جوړ شي.

2. Investment

In the five-year period total investment (Investment) of eight trillion (i.e. eighty kharab) rupees will be required, which will increase from 16.8 per cent of GDP in 2004-05 to 20.7 per cent in 2009-10. Sixty-five per cent of investment will be in the private sector (Private Sector) and thirty-five per cent in the government sector (Public Sector). 88.3 per cent of this investment will consist of the internal savings (Internal Savings) of the country and twelve per cent of foreign resources (Foreign Resources).

3. Balance of foreign payments (Balance of Foreign Payments)

To make the balance of foreign payments better, during the plan an effort will be made that variety and diversification (Diversification) be created in exports. Further, stability be created in the rate of exchange (Exchange Rate), and the ability to compete be created in exports (Exports).

4. Public sector development programme (PSDP)

Under the development programme of the government sector, investment of a total of 2042 billion rupees will be made. As it were, compared with 2004-05, in 2009-10 this will increase threefold and will be 6.3 per cent of GDP. This sum will be spent on these sectors: energy, communications, news-giving, water resources, education, vocational training, public health, physical (Physical) planning and housing.

5. Poverty reduction

At this time one-third (i.e. 33 per cent) of the total population of Pakistan is living below the poverty line (Poverty Line). Under the new plan, by 2010 a reduction of twenty-one per cent will be made in poverty, and in this connection too the following strategy will be adopted:

1. Stress on schemes for getting employment for the poor.

2. Increase in the rate of economic growth (Growth Rate) of the sectors of agriculture, small businesses and construction.

3. Stress on programmes of relief for the poor in connection with Khushhal Pakistan, Tameer-e-Pakistan and drought etc.

4. Issuing small loans (Micro Credits) to agriculture and small businesses.

5. Social protection.

6. More attention to the development of human resources (Human Resources), i.e. education and health.

7. Allotting government lands to landless (Landless) rural people.

6. Housing

At this time in Pakistan there are sixty lakh houses fewer than needed, and by 2010 the need for a further thirty lakh houses will arise. As it were, every year the need for five lakh seventy thousand more houses arises, whereas only three lakh new houses are prepared annually. Therefore during the plan an effort will be made that:

1. The provision of long-term loans at a fixed rate through financial institutions for the construction of houses be made easy.

2. Small residential plots be prepared for people with low income.

3. The technology of house construction be made better.
